common_name: Florence Vaughan Canna (Classic Yellow Red-Spotted Heirloom Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions after the last frost, 3-4 inches deep in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun; this nineteenth-century heirloom has remained in continuous cultivation longer than almost any other canna.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3 to 4 inches deep in fertile, consistently moist soil in full sun after the last frost. Florence Vaughan is a long-cultivated heirloom canna dating to the 1890s, bearing bold golden-yellow flowers heavily speckled and blotched in red across each petal, carried well above broad, clean green foliage from midsummer until frost. Its vigor and reliable performance in heat and humidity have kept it in continuous nursery trade longer than almost any other named canna. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring, and in regions colder than zone 7, lift rhizomes after frost blackens the foliage and store them in a cool, frost-free place over winter.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions after the last frost, 3-4 inches deep in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun; America pairs dark bronze-red foliage with bright red flowers for strong color contrast all season.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3 to 4 inches deep in fertile, consistently moist soil in full sun after the last frost. America is an early-1900s heirloom canna prized for the contrast between its deep bronze-red, almost maroon foliage and its clear, bright red flowers, a combination that still reads as striking more than a century after its introduction. It grows into a sturdy, upright clump that holds up well in summer heat and humidity, flowering continuously from midsummer into fall. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring, and in regions colder than zone 7, lift rhizomes after frost blackens the foliage and store them in a cool, frost-free place over winter.

common_name: Cannova Yellow Canna (Seed-Grown Compact Yellow Canna)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost after nicking or soaking the hard seed coat to speed germination, then transplant into full sun after frost danger passes; Cannova is a seed-grown series bred for uniform, compact garden performance.

directions: Nick or soak the hard seed coat before sowing indoors, since this speeds and evens out an otherwise slow germination, then transplant into fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun once frost danger has passed. Cannova Yellow is part of a seed-propagated canna series bred for compact, uniform garden habit and clean, clear-yellow flowers without the red speckling typical of older heirloom cannas, blooming heavily from early summer through frost. Its shorter stature compared to many heirloom cannas suits mixed beds and large containers without the need for staking. Keep soil consistently moist through the growing season, since cannas are heavy water users, and in regions colder than zone 7 either treat as an annual or lift rhizomes for winter storage after frost.

common_name: Cannova Mango Canna (Seed-Grown Compact Orange Canna)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost after nicking or soaking the hard seed coat, then transplant into full sun after frost danger passes; a compact, uniform seed-grown Cannova series selection in warm orange tones.

directions: Nick or soak the hard seed coat before sowing indoors to speed and even out germination, then transplant into fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun once frost danger has passed. Cannova Mango carries warm orange flowers over clean green foliage on a compact, uniform plant, part of the same seed-propagated series as Cannova Yellow and bred for garden-ready performance without the variability of older seed-grown cannas. It blooms continuously from early summer through frost and holds up well in heat and humidity, making it a dependable choice for mixed sunny beds and large patio containers. Keep soil consistently moist, since cannas use water heavily, and in regions colder than zone 7 either treat as an annual or lift and store rhizomes over winter.

common_name: Toucan Rose Canna (Compact Rose-Pink Vegetative Canna)

planting.note: Plant divisions or started plants after the last frost in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun; Toucan Rose is a compact, early-flowering vegetatively propagated canna bred for containers and small beds.

directions: Plant divisions or started plants in fertile, consistently moist soil in full sun after the last frost. Toucan Rose is a compact, early-to-flower canna from a vegetatively propagated series bred for strong garden performance in a shorter stature than older heirloom types, bearing clear rose-pink blooms over clean green foliage from early summer through frost. Its reduced height suits mixed sunny borders and large containers without staking, and it keeps flowering steadily through summer heat and humidity. Keep soil consistently moist, since cannas are heavy water users, and in regions colder than zone 7 lift rhizomes after frost blackens the foliage and store them in a cool, frost-free place over winter.

planting.note: Plant bulbs with the neck at or just above soil level in spring in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun to partial shade; this long-cultivated garden hybrid spider lily is sterile and propagates only by bulb division.

directions: Plant bulbs with the neck at or just above soil level in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun to partial shade. This long-cultivated garden hybrid spider lily produces large, fragrant white flowers with the narrow, spidery petal-like segments typical of Hymenocallis, carried in clusters atop sturdy stalks above strap-shaped evergreen foliage in warm climates, with flowering concentrated in summer. Because it is a sterile hybrid, it spreads only by offset bulbs rather than seed, forming slowly expanding clumps over the years. It thrives in the humid heat of the Gulf Coast and tolerates both consistently moist beds and brief dry spells once established, needing winter protection or indoor overwintering outside the warmest zones.

planting.note: Plant bulbs 1-2 inches deep in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this Gulf South native rain lily flowers in flushes after warm-season rain events rather than on a fixed schedule.

directions: Plant bulbs 1 to 2 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade. Prairie rain lily is a small bulb native to Texas, Louisiana, and adjacent Gulf South states, sending up clusters of narrow grass-like leaves and surprising flushes of pale pink to white, funnel-shaped flowers within days of a warm-season rain, a bloom pattern shared with its Zephyranthes relatives. It naturalizes readily in lawns, rock gardens, and border edges in the warm, humid climate of its native range, multiplying by bulb offsets into expanding colonies over time. It tolerates both regular garden watering and the dry spells typical of its native prairie and savanna habitats, needing winter protection or a dry mulch covering outside the warmest part of its hardiness range.
